findings.evidence:
- New behavior: `BuildIndexInfo` sets `idxInfo.Global` only from `indexOption.Global` (`pkg/ddl/index.go:317`, `pkg/ddl/index.go:357`).
- Job arg decoding no longer reads the trailing legacy `global` bool (`pkg/ddl/index.go:564`, `pkg/ddl/index.go:579`).
- Yet DDL jobs still carry a trailing `global` arg (now always `false`) (`pkg/ddl/executor.go:4541`, `pkg/ddl/executor.go:4697`).
- First-parent code used that trailing `global` bool to set `IndexInfo.Global` (`4764397725a7381d9424fef14c812192fe7441fa:pkg/ddl/index.go:344`) and decoded it from RawArgs (`4764397725a7381d9424fef14c812192fe7441fa:pkg/ddl/index.go:582`).
- `Job.DecodeArgs` truncates to the number of decode targets, so an extra legacy arg can be silently ignored when no longer decoded (`pkg/parser/model/ddl.go:767`).
findings.fix: When decoding add-index / add-PK jobs, if the legacy trailing `global` arg exists and is `true`, propagate it into the new representation (e.g. initialize `indexOption` if nil and set `indexOption.Global=true`, or explicitly set `indexInfo.Global` from legacy arg for v1 jobs). Also consider setting the legacy `global` arg to `indexOption.Global` when enqueueing, to preserve mixed-version owner safety.
findings.impact: Rolling upgrade / owner switch while an *old-format* DDL job is queued (or before it has appended the index into `tblInfo.Indices`) can create a **local** unique index instead of a **global** one on a partitioned table. That can silently weaken uniqueness guarantees across partitions (allowing duplicates and inconsistent metadata vs user intent).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Up to `upstream/master`, legacy v1 job arg `Global` is explicitly marked unused (`upstream/master:pkg/meta/model/job_args.go:1383`), and index building still uses `IndexOption.Global` via `BuildIndexInfo` (called from `checkAndBuildIndexInfo`) without consuming the legacy bool (`upstream/master:pkg/ddl/index.go:805`, `upstream/master:pkg/ddl/index.go:839`).
findings.verify:
1) On pre-#55264 TiDB, enqueue (but do not let complete) `ALTER TABLE p ADD UNIQUE INDEX idx(a)` on a partitioned table with `tidb_enable_global_index=ON` where `a` doesn’t include all partitioning columns.
2) Upgrade to this commit while the job is still pending in `ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS`.
3) Let the job run and verify `information_schema.tidb_indexes` / table meta shows `IndexInfo.Global=true` (or job is rejected), and uniqueness is enforced across partitions (duplicates across partitions should fail).
findings.what: Forward-compat regression for in-flight DDL jobs: old queued add-index / add-primary-key jobs that relied on the legacy job-arg `global` boolean may be executed with `IndexInfo.Global=false` after this commit, because the worker no longer decodes/uses the legacy `global` flag and instead derives `IndexInfo.Global` solely from `IndexOption.Global`.

subject: *: Require GLOBAL IndexOption for creating Global Index (#55264)
summary: Requires explicit `GLOBAL` IndexOption when a unique key on a partitioned table doesn’t include all partitioning columns; adds `UPDATE INDEXES` handling for partition reorg and shifts `IndexInfo.Global` derivation to `ast.IndexOption.Global` (legacy job-arg `global` is effectively deprecated).
